CVX.rationale: Chevron's fundamental health and trajectory are deteriorating sharply. Q1 2026 showed EPS of $1.11, down 44.5% YoY from $2.00, with operating cash flow collapsing 51.6% to $2.51B. The quarterly trajectory is non-contiguous (Q1,Q3,Q2,Q1) making TTM unreliable, but the most recent quarter shows severe margin compression: net margin fell to 5.9% from 7.8% a year ago, operating margin at 9.5%, and ROE collapsed to 5.9% from 10.5%. Valuation is extremely stretched: P/E of 30.4x is near the top of its 16-35 range over the past year, having expanded from 16x in June 2025 despite earnings declining. P/B of 1.8x is mid-range but supported by a balance sheet that saw total equity decline from $195.6B to $189.4B QoQ. The stock has already declined 16% in the past quarter from $205 to $172, yet remains expensive relative to deteriorating fundamentals. Oil prices have crashed 30% from $105 to $73/bbl (WTI), directly threatening Chevron's upstream earnings. The U.S.-Iran peace deal reopening the Strait of Hormuz removes the geopolitical premium that had supported oil prices. While the Microsoft data center deal is a positive long-term growth platform, it's modest relative to Chevron's scale and won't offset near-term earnings headwinds. The Hess acquisition integration adds production but also complexity and legal risk from Exxon's arbitration claim. Dividend coverage is strained with earnings yield at only 3.3%. No credible near-term fundamental catalyst exists to re-rate the stock higher; the next earnings event will likely show continued pressure from lower oil prices.
